recent_posts.title: Issue #198 · WebAssembly Weekly
recent_posts.summary: The 2023 state of WebAssembly survey results reveal interesting trends in language usage, with Rust and JavaScript seeing increased adoption. Developers desire languages like Zig, Kotlin, and C#. WebAssembly is commonly used for web development, but serverless and plugin environments are on the rise. Threads, garbage collection, and the component model proposal are the most anticipated WebAssembly developments.

recent_posts.title: Issue #197 · WebAssembly Weekly
recent_posts.summary: WebAssembly has grown considerably and is being used for diverse applications. The 2022 survey showed increasing usage of Rust and Python, JavaScript becoming a viable WebAssembly language, and more. VectorVisor is a tool that runs WebAssembly programs on GPUs. Carnegie Mellon University has launched a research center dedicated to WebAssembly. The Raverie Engine recreates the Flash experience of old.

recent_posts.title: Issue #196 · WebAssembly Weekly
recent_posts.summary: Learn how to write WebAssembly directly and explore its potential. Discover how Haskell can be used with WebAssembly. Understand the similarities between WebAssembly and the Unix philosophy. Explore NGINX Unit's support for WebAssembly and its unique APIs for exposing HTTP requests. Watch a video that provides an introduction to the history and capabilities of WebAssembly.

recent_posts.title: Issue #194 · WebAssembly Weekly
recent_posts.summary: The Bytecode Alliance was announced four years ago as an industry partnership working together to create the specifications and tooling needed to run WebAssembly outside of the browser. This blog post gives a snapshot of their current activities and roadmap. It is cleat that there is a lot going on at the moment, and much to get excited about.

recent_posts.title: Issue #193 · WebAssembly Weekly
recent_posts.summary: Wasm NEVERSAW.US is a software runtime that executes WebAssembly modules with sandboxing, task orchestration, and time travel capabilities. This is part one of a series, part two is here, with a combined reading time of about 70 minutes, this is practically a book already! I applaud the authors dedication.

recent_posts.title: Issue #192 · WebAssembly Weekly
recent_posts.summary: Polywasm is an implementation of a WebAssembly virtual machine, in JavaScript, which you can use as a polyfill. This isn’t the first of its kind, webassemblyjs released a similar wasm interpreter, a couple of years ago. Wasmati gives an alternative for people wanting to hand-craft their WebAssembly modules.

recent_posts.title: Issue #65 · WebAssembly Weekly
recent_posts.summary: ME WebRTC is a Google-backed project, and W3C standard, that has been active for the last eight years. It is developing peer-to-peer communications between browsers - for example allowing direct audio / video chat from one browser to another.

recent_posts.title: Issue #132 · WebAssembly Weekly
recent_posts.summary: The article charts Marcel's journey into WebAssembly, starting with C++/Emscripten which he found promising, but the file size was too bloated. In his next experiment he gave AssemblyScript, which yielded a much more compact result. The article also looks at various ways to connect WebAssembly to the host JavaScript APIs.

recent_posts.title: Issue #14 · WebAssembly Weekly
recent_posts.summary: This blog post describes the process of porting a C++ barcode scanner project, ZXing, to WebAssembly using Emscripten. This really interesting presentation, from Lin Clark, who is famed for her code cartoons, looks at how React might make use of WebAssembly in the future.

top_posts.title: Issue #183 · WebAssembly Weekly
top_posts.summary: WebAssembly is a complex and powerful tool for the web. Adobe are also very interested in how they can leverage WebAssembly on the server-side. This blog post details some recent projects where they have been looking at how to incorporate WebAssembly into their existing Kubernetes-based architecture.
